summary: The registered universal_address_writer_equivariance preserves universal admission/post-state renaming over four source-shaped writer projections and adds LiveClaimBatchBehavior over arbitrary callee/context/request/hint/recipient/world inputs. Actual root success derives an ordered physical claim/CALL/event chain; root failure restores the entire modeled caller/callee world. The live execution limb has no supplied admission boolean or stage-success premise. Global caller/owner/callee-world renaming is not proved. Claim storage now enters and commits the executing account frame; its storage-stage effects preserve foreign-account words before the recipient callback.

classification.work: Preserve the registered universal writer theorem, allowance-before-balance and owner-before-hint guard order, physical AccountFrame claim connection, recipient/precompile call dispatch and whole-world rollback. These are implemented components, not future inversion tasks. Remaining work: derive whole-world renaming across all writers and their physical storage/callees, preserve designated precompile behavior under the intended address relation, and connect runtime/deployment and event/ABI observations without singleton-actor restrictions.

next_gate: OPEN: validate the strengthened registered parent and live-call regressions, then independently audit the actual physical claim/CALL/rollback composition. Global live-world renaming and the named deployed/external-interface obligations remain open; do not promote projection or legacy-journal results to those claims.

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1.universal_address_writer_equivariance
theorems.doc:
/-- Two nonzero callers have the same source-shaped admission bit, and a
successful post-state renames under the swap.

Registered P-ADDRESS-1 parent. For two nonzero callers, the source-shaped
`run` admits `a₁` iff it admits `a₂` on the caller-swapped input, and a
successful post-state renames under the same swap. The claim is unconditional
over four modeled address-bearing writer projections: since wave 5,
`addressEquivarianceEntryScope` covers `claimWithdrawalsTo` too -- its
request-owner gate (`caller = requestOwner`) is caller-relative and renames
with the caller (`requestOwner` is an address-indexed input field renamed by
`renameInput`) -- so the scope is total over the modeled writers
(`addressEquivarianceEntryScope_total`). The wave-4 scope premise thereby
became vacuous: the source lemmas below hold for every `EntryPoint` via
`run_rename`, so the premise's deletion cannot break the proof, and per the
wave-4 load-bearing criterion it is no longer carried. On
`requestWithdrawals` and `unwrap`, admission is pause plus the caller's own
balance/allowance flags only (`pause_balance_admitted_is_permissionless`); it
does not test `caller = owner` or `caller = <fixed constant>`. Adding a
fixed-owner gate to that admission breaks equivariance via
`LidoSRv3.Tests.AddressSourceMutants.fixed_owner_gate_kill_line_refutes_parent`,
which negates this theorem's exact predicate shape on a mutant of this file's
own `admitted`/`run`/`renameInput` (not an unrelated toy entrypoint).

`wellFormedAddressInput` and `singletonActorEntryPoint` are deliberately not
carried as hypotheses here: neither restricts this conclusion (the proof
below needs only `a₁, a₂ ≠ 0`), and `singletonActorEntryPoint` is provably
`False` for every `EntryPoint` in this model
(`not_singleton_actor_entry_point`), so requiring its negation would add no
content while reading as a real exclusion. Carrying either as an unused
binder would hide that they are premise-free rather than making the claim
more honest. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem universal_address_writer_equivariance
    (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address) (h₁ : a₁ ≠ 0) (h₂ : a₂ ≠ 0)
    (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input) :
    (AdmissionIsCallerBlind a₁ a₂ inp ∧ PostStateRenamesWithCaller a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
      LiveClaimBatchBehavior

theorems.role: registered Verity Executable Contract parent (audit/guarantees.yaml verity.theorem)
theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1.abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance
theorems.doc:
/-- Two nonzero callers have the same source-shaped admission bit, and a
successful post-state renames under the swap. Verity composition adds
`Contract.run` observe = `sourceAddressView` when the amount fits one word
and the balance/allowance flags are coherent, snapshot rollback on revert, and
the renamed run observing the renamed view.

Composition of (i) the universal source-shaped swap, (ii) each
`Contract.run` entrypoint's address-write `observe` matching
`sourceAddressView` when `amount < 2^256` and the balance/allowance
flags are coherent, (iii) any `Contract.run` revert restoring the
snapshot, (iv) the renamed input's TX view matching `postAddressView`
of the renamed post-state. Not a WQ claim. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance :
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      AdmissionIsCallerBlind a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      PostStateRenamesWithCaller a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
    (∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      AmountFitsWord inp → BalanceFlagCoherent inp → AllowanceFlagCoherent inp →
      ObservesSourceView inp) ∧
    RevertRestoresSnapshot ∧
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input) (post : PostState),
      LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.run inp = .committed post →
      AmountFitsWord inp → BalanceFlagCoherent inp → AllowanceFlagCoherent inp →
      RenamedRunObservesRenamedView a₁ a₂ inp post)

assumptions.risk: Canonical runtime, codehash, fork configuration, and address provenance are unavailable in general; Mock-derived evidence is non-production evidence. Chantier 4 (Thomas 2026-09-13) narrows this for two deployed-runtime fixtures under `fixtures/deployed/` to exact identifiers: `WithdrawalVault_implementation` at `0xfB4521BD151BFB45DB6045D2d07e58e0f597e340` with EIP-1052 codehash `0xd1e0d1b48e4f5abd04bdfd14805366f0cf7946b7bb41b7a5ad8652361f3e3d36` (mainnet, block-independent at any block where the immutable code has not been upgraded — the implementation slot on the WithdrawalVault_proxy `0xB9D7934878B5FB9610B3fE8A5e441e8fad7E293f` points at this deployed runtime, and the runtime is not upgradeable); `StakingRouter_implementation` at `0xDD76927045435C7605cf6f5F978cfb8CABDb5F80` with codehash `0x9cd5d45ddde5f74d3867aa22c98fd79a85df89d202145bc588173d92e00600ec` (same block-independence rationale). Under `ETH_RPC_URL`, the `verify_*_immutable.py` scripts re-fetch and re-verify against the live chain, so a mismatch fails the build; without `ETH_RPC_URL`, they enforce the pinned codehash. For every other contract or configuration under this assumption, the generic reduction stands.
assumptions.justification: This premise isolates an unproved environment or representation fact instead of hiding it in the theorem. Chantier 4 (Thomas 2026-09-13) narrows this for the two deployed-runtime fixtures under `fixtures/deployed/` by recording their exact EIP-1052 EXTCODEHASH (keccak256 of the runtime bytecode) in `audit/artifacts.lock.json`: `WithdrawalVault_implementation` (0xfB4521BD151BFB45DB6045D2d07e58e0f597e340) codehash = 0xd1e0d1b48e4f5abd04bdfd14805366f0cf7946b7bb41b7a5ad8652361f3e3d36, `StakingRouter_implementation` (0xDD76927045435C7605cf6f5F978cfb8CABDb5F80) codehash = 0x9cd5d45ddde5f74d3867aa22c98fd79a85df89d202145bc588173d92e00600ec. That is the exact identifier `EXTCODEHASH <implementation>` on any Ethereum node returns for either implementation at any block where the code has not been upgraded. The `verify_*_immutable.py` scripts (invoked from `make test`) recompute keccak256 of the fixture and reject any mismatch; under `ETH_RPC_URL` they also refetch and re-verify against the live chain.
assumptions.violation_impact: Any guarantee linked to this premise must be re-evaluated if the premise is false.
assumptions.validation: Applies to every guarantee. scripts/check_deployed_code.py reads each proxy implementation slot, hashes the on-chain bytecode and compares the verified source with the pinned lido-core checkout; PROVENANCE.md explains the procedure. Chantier 4 additions: for the two deployed-runtime fixtures the exact EIP-1052 codehash is recorded (see `justification`) and enforced by `scripts/verify_beacon_deposit_immutable.py`, `scripts/verify_consolidation_request_immutable.py`, and `scripts/verify_deposit_thirty_two_ether.py` (all three are `make test` targets). A mismatch between the recomputed keccak256 and the recorded codehash fails the build; `ETH_RPC_URL` enables live re-verification against the current chain state.
assumptions.removal_path: Replace the premise with a machine-checked correspondence theorem or a narrower proved interface. Chantier 4 (Thomas 2026-09-13) narrows the runtime-identity strand for two deployed fixtures to the exact EIP-1052 codehash values above; historical block-number binding and the remaining contracts remain follow-up work.

covered: Original universal source-shaped admission/post-state equivariance over transferFrom, requestWithdrawals, claimWithdrawalsTo and unwrap, without adding singleton-actor entrypoints; permissionless pause/balance/allowance admission is established only for requestWithdrawals and unwrap.

Registered LiveClaimBatchBehavior cases on runClaimWithdrawalsTo actual root outcome over arbitrary worlds and request/hint lists. Successful execution derives recipient and length guards and ClaimChain; failed execution restores the complete input world.

Each ClaimChain step derives packed owner/claimed/finalized checks, actual physical keccak queue/checkpoint/EnumerableSet reads and checked writes, source-computed payout and locked-ETH subtraction, funded recipient/value/empty-calldata CALL, callback-returned world/data/nested attempts, and ordered WithdrawalClaimed then Transfer events.

PayoutEffect exposes the provisional sender debit/recipient credit and either EOA success or the precise external-callee returned world. Later claims use that returned world, so earlier callback effects participate in whole-batch rollback.

Projection guard order follows the relevant source order: finalized before claimed/owner and owner before hint for claims; stETH allowance before balance for request transferFrom. The physical claim already checks recipient before array length and marks/removes the owned request before hint/payout calculation.

Parent-shaped admission and owner-write mutants retain the strengthened live conjunct while falsifying the source renaming conjunct. PackDAddressClaimMutants exercises actual CALL order/target, zero-recipient rejection, and root rollback.
Four source-shaped storage-writing Contract.run entrypoints retain their existing address-write observable correspondences; these remain separate from the actual callee-world execution plane.
missing: Global live-state equivariance: no theorem relates two executions after jointly renaming sender, packed owners, owner-indexed sets, balances, code and arbitrary callee behavior. The retained source-projection equivariance does not discharge this obligation.

General deployed EVM refinement: physical slot formulas are executable and used directly, but World.core is the active-contract storage model. No full deployment/runtime/interpreter correspondence or arbitrary external-code correctness is supplied; External is the named executable callee interface.

Arbitrary successful callbacks may spend their credited ETH or modify claim storage. Final recipient net credit and final claimed-bit preservation are not asserted; the precise returned world is retained instead.

Other writer bodies: the four-input projection still carries environment booleans. Full requestWithdrawals/unwrap/token-transfer and ERC-721 approval-branch state/callee equivariance is not established by the claim-batch limb.

Legacy AddressClaimJournalLegacy and BatchReady recipient-renaming results are historical journal evidence, not physical-storage or arbitrary-callback proofs. PAddress1BridgeCallPremise naming/projection helpers do not derive actual callee behavior and are not consumed as closure.
